Um, and so after we have an audit plan and we are performing the actual audit, uh, there are four or three phases, uh, during the audit. Um, phase one is planning, uh, phase two is fieldwork, and phase three is reporting.

So in phase one of planning, the audit has already commenced, and we are meeting with, um, stakeholders and owner, process owners to go over, um, their duties and responsibilities for us to gain an understanding of their tasks and their job duties. Um, the planning section, i-it says planning, but it is actual audits in progress. It is not us gearing up to do the audit. It is us performing the audit to determine the

testing steps that we will perform during the audit. Uh, once we have done that, we use that information, uh, to develop a risk-based testing program. Uh, we will then per-perform testing, which we call fieldwork, to see

if we are operating as intended per the criteria set forth in our policies and regulations at the state and federal level. Uh, once we perform those steps, uh, we then will move on to the reporting phase, which includes exit meetings, uh, and discussions with the process owners who were audited during that period. Um, once we have met with those individuals, uh, we will then draft

an audit report. Uh, when we draft an audit report, we provide that back to management, so they can provide responses. Uh, and those responses may include corrections to our audit findings.
